cards.title: Crossing safely
facts: In India vehicles drive on the left, so traffic first comes from your right.
Many pedestrian accidents happen when people step out from between parked vehicles.
Phones and earphones hide traffic sounds.
do: Use zebra crossings, subways or footbridges
Stop at the kerb, look right, left and right again
Cross when the road is clear or vehicles have stopped
Walk, don't run, and keep looking
dont: Don't use your phone or earphones while crossing

myths.statement: At a zebra crossing, all vehicles always stop, so you don't need to look.
myths.truth: Many drivers don't stop. Always look and make eye contact before crossing.

quiz.q: At a zebra crossing with no signal, what should you do before crossing?
options: Run across quickly
Stop, look right, left and right again
Cross while looking at your phone
Wait for a friend to go first
quiz.explanation: Look both ways and cross only when it's clear or vehicles have stopped.

situations: After school, {name} and {relation} need to cross a busy road to reach {the}. The zebra crossing is 50 metres away, but there's a gap between two parked autos right in front of them.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Walk to the zebra crossing / safe crossing point
rubric.note: Crossings are where drivers expect you.
Drivers can't see you step out.

rubric.point: Stop, look right-left-right and cross when clear
rubric.note: Traffic first comes from the right in India.

rubric.point: No phone or earphones; hold a younger child's hand

cards.title: Helping at a road accident
facts: Moving an injured person can make a spine injury worse.
Removing a helmet can worsen a neck injury.
India's Good Samaritan rules protect people who help accident victims in good faith.
112 is India's single emergency number; 108 is the ambulance number in many states.
do: Make sure you are safe first
Warn traffic (hazard lights, warning triangle, a helper waving)
Keep the injured person still and talk to them calmly
dont: Don't move the injured person unless there is immediate danger like fire
Don't remove a helmet unless they can't breathe

myths.statement: If you help someone after an accident, the police will trouble you.
myths.truth: Good Samaritan rules protect people who help in good faith. You won't be forced to give personal details.

quiz.q: You're first to reach a bike accident on a busy road. The rider is awake but can't stand. What do you do first?
options: Lift them into a car and rush to hospital
Make the spot safe from traffic, then call 112
Take off their helmet so they can breathe
Give them water and help them sit up
quiz.explanation: Moving an injured person can make spine injuries worse, and a helmet should stay on unless they can't breathe. Make the scene safe, call 112, and stay with them. Good Samaritan rules protect people who help.

quiz.q: After a crash, a conscious biker is lying on the road. Should you take their helmet off?
options: Yes, right away so they can breathe
No. Leave it on unless they can't breathe
Only if they ask you to
Yes, then help them sit up
quiz.explanation: Removing a helmet can worsen a neck injury. Keep them still and call 112.

quiz.q: Which number works for any emergency in India?
quiz.explanation: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

situations: {name} is the first to reach a bike accident on a busy road near {the}. The rider is awake but can't stand. {relation} wants to lift the rider into a car.
scenario.question: What should {name} do first?
scenario.bubble: Let's lift him into the car!

rubric.point: Make the scene safe and warn traffic
rubric.note: Protect yourself and the victim from other vehicles.

rubric.point: Don't move them or remove the helmet
rubric.note: Moving can worsen spine and neck injuries.

rubric.point: Stay with them and keep them calm

cards.title: Cycling safely
facts: Most cycling falls happen close to home on short rides.
A helmet only protects when it fits and the strap is fastened.
Riding with the flow of traffic makes you more visible and predictable.
do: Wear a helmet every ride, strap fastened
Ride on the left, with traffic
Use lights and reflectors at night
dont: Don't ride with earphones or a phone
Don't carry a friend on the carrier or crossbar

myths.statement: You only need a helmet on long rides or highways.
myths.truth: Most falls happen on short rides near home. Wear it every time.

quiz.q: When is a bicycle helmet most useful?
options: Only on highways
Only when racing
Every ride, even short ones
Only at night
quiz.explanation: Wear it on every ride, strap fastened.

cards.title: School bus safety
facts: Drivers of large vehicles have big blind spots right in front of and behind them.
Most bus-stop injuries happen while getting on or off.
do: Wait away from the road edge
Get on and off only when the bus has fully stopped
Cross only where the driver can see you, after the bus has moved
dont: Don't run after a moving bus
Don't jump off before it stops

myths.statement: It's okay to jump off the bus just before it stops if you're careful.
myths.truth: Wait for a full stop. Moving vehicles throw you off balance.

quiz.q: Where is the safest place to get off a school bus?
options: Anywhere the bus slows down
Only at the stop, after the bus has fully stopped
From the back door in traffic
Jump off before it stops to save time
quiz.explanation: Wait for a full stop at the bus stop, then move away from the bus before crossing.
